title: g·A ∩ A is a cellular subcomplex of A
body_html:
$g \cdot A \cap A$ is a cellular subcomplex of $A$

Lemma. For any $g \in G$, the intersection $g \cdot A \cap A$ is a cellular subcomplex of $A$.
proof_html:
By the cell intersection lemma from CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' applied to $X = \BSigma$, $g \cdot A \cap A$ is a union of facets in $\mathscr{F}$. For any two facets $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}' \in \mathscr{F}$ with $\mathcal{F} = g \mathcal{F}' \subseteq g \cdot A \cap A$, the QFD property gives $n \in N$ with $n \cdot \mathcal{F}' = \mathcal{F}$. Then $gA \supseteq \partial(g\mathcal{F}') = \partial(n\mathcal{F}') = n\partial\mathcal{F}' = \partial\mathcal{F}$, so the boundary of every facet of the intersection is again in the intersection. Hence it is a subcomplex. $\square$

This compatibility of apartments is the geometric input for the contraction extension argument (see [[node:building.contraction_extension_K3]]).
